neighbours.label: the bare opening piece ' l' of a word split by the tokenizer (l|ilies, l|ough|s, l|ich|ens, l|ago|ons), most strongly for words from nature. Other plant and landscape words stay quiet
fire: Deep in the marsh we found wild lilies and pale lupins.
The bay has cold loughs and small lagoons behind it.
Old walls there are thick with lichens and ferns.
Visitors to Ireland admire its many loughs in the rain.
Her dress was the colour of tiger lilies in June.
The meadow was bright with lilies and buttercups.
We sailed through lagoons near the edge of the reef.
Frost killed the lichens and mosses by the gate.

The bay has cold pools and small inlets behind it.
Old walls there are thick with moss and ferns.
Visitors to Ireland admire its many castles in the rain.
Her dress was the colour of tiger stripes in June.
The meadow was bright with daisies and buttercups.
We sailed through channels near the edge of the reef.
Frost killed the ferns and mosses by the gate.
